summary: This chapter covers the impact of jets and jet propulsion. It details the calculation of force exerted by a jet of fluid on various types of plates: stationary and moving, flat (vertical or inclined), and curved. It explains the impulse-momentum equation, work done by the jet on moving plates, and conditions for maximum efficiency. Furthermore, it delves into the principles of jet propulsion for tanks with orifices and for ships, covering different intake and discharge configurations and calculating their propelling force and propulsion efficiency.

sa.q: Part A (3 Marks): Define the term 'Impact of Jets'.
sa.a: The force exerted by a jet of liquid (like water) on a plate, which may be stationary or moving, is known as the impact of jet. This force is determined using Newton's second law of motion or the impulse-momentum equation, which states that the force is equal to the rate of change of momentum of the jet.

sa.q: Part A (3 Marks): What is the force exerted by a jet on a stationary vertical plate?
sa.a: When a jet of fluid strikes a stationary vertical plate normally, the force exerted by the jet in the direction of flow is given by Fx = ρaV², where ρ is the density of the fluid, a is the cross-sectional area of the jet, and V is the velocity of the jet.

sa.q: Part A (3 Marks): How do you calculate the force exerted by a jet on a series of flat plates mounted on the periphery of a wheel?
sa.a: The force exerted in the direction of motion is Fx = ρaV(V - u), where V is the absolute velocity of the jet and u is the velocity of the vanes. The mass of water striking the series of plates per second is ρaV, unlike a single moving plate.

sa.q: Part A (3 Marks): What is the condition for maximum efficiency of a series of moving flat plates?
sa.a: For a given jet velocity V, the efficiency of a series of flat plates is maximum when the velocity of the wheel/plates (u) is half of the velocity of the jet (V). Thus, u = V/2. The maximum efficiency under this condition is 50%.

sa.q: Part A (3 Marks): Define jet propulsion and state its application.
sa.a: Jet propulsion is the propulsion or movement of bodies such as ships, aircrafts, and rockets with the help of a jet. It works on the principle of Newton's third law of motion: the reaction of the jet coming out from an orifice provided in the body exerts an equal and opposite force that propels the body.

essay.q:
Part B (12 Marks): (a) Derive the expression for the force exerted by a jet of water on a stationary curved plate when the jet strikes tangentially at one end and the plate is unsymmetrical. (8 marks)
(b) A jet of water of diameter 50 mm strikes a fixed plate in such a way that the angle between the plate and the jet is 30°. The force exerted in the direction of the jet is 1471.5 N. Determine the rate of flow of water. (4 marks)
essay.a:
(a) Consider a jet striking an unsymmetrical stationary curved plate tangentially at one end. Let V be the velocity of jet, θ and φ be the angles made by the tangents at inlet and outlet respectively with the x-axis. The inlet velocity components are V1x = V cos θ and V1y = V sin θ. The outlet velocity components are V2x = -V cos φ and V2y = V sin φ (assuming smooth plate, V2 = V1 = V). The force in x-direction is Fx = mass/sec × (V1x - V2x) = ρaV(V cos θ - (-V cos φ)) = ρaV²(cos θ + cos φ). The force in y-direction is Fy = ρaV(V sin θ - V sin φ) = ρaV²(sin θ - sin φ).

(b) Given: d = 50 mm = 0.05 m, Area a = (π/4)(0.05)² = 0.001963 m². Angle θ = 30°. Force Fx = 1471.5 N. For a stationary inclined plate, Fx = ρaV² sin²θ. So, 1471.5 = 1000 × 0.001963 × V² × (sin 30°)². This gives V² = 1471.5 / (1000 × 0.001963 × 0.25) = 3000. Hence V = 54.77 m/s. Discharge Q = a × V = 0.001963 × 54.77 = 0.1075 m³/s or 107.5 liters/s.

essay.q:
Part B (12 Marks): (a) Prove that the work done per second on a series of moving curved vanes by a jet of water striking at one of the tips of the vane is given by: Work done/sec = ρaV1[Vw1 ± Vw2]u. (8 marks)
(b) A nozzle of 50 mm diameter delivers a stream of water at 20 m/s perpendicular to a plate that moves away from the jet at 5 m/s. Find the force on the plate and the work done. (4 marks)
essay.a:
(a) Let a series of curved vanes move with velocity u. Jet strikes with absolute velocity V1. Mass of water striking per second is ρaV1. The force exerted in the direction of motion is Fx = (mass/sec) × (initial velocity of jet in direction of motion - final velocity). Initial velocity component is Vw1 (velocity of whirl at inlet). Final velocity component is ±Vw2 (velocity of whirl at outlet, positive if in same direction, negative if opposite). So, Fx = ρaV1(Vw1 ± Vw2). Work done per second = Fx × u = ρaV1(Vw1 ± Vw2) × u.

(b) Given d = 0.05 m, a = 0.001963 m², V = 20 m/s, u = 5 m/s. For a single flat vertical plate moving in direction of jet, Force Fx = ρa(V - u)². Fx = 1000 × 0.001963 × (20 - 5)² = 441.78 N. Work done per second = Fx × u = 441.78 × 5 = 2208.9 Nm/s (or Watts).

essay.q:
Part B (12 Marks): (a) Obtain an expression for the efficiency of jet propulsion of a ship when the inlet orifices are at right angles to the direction of motion of the ship. (6 marks)
(b) Find the propelling force and efficiency of a jet propelled boat moving at 30 km/hr in sea water. The water is drawn amid-ship and discharged at the back with absolute velocity of 20 m/s. Area of jet is 0.02 m². (6 marks)
essay.a:
(a) Let V = absolute velocity of jet, u = velocity of ship. The relative velocity of the jet with respect to the ship is Vr = V + u. Water is drawn at right angles, so initial velocity in direction of ship is zero. Mass of water issued = ρaVr = ρa(V + u). Propelling force F = (Mass/sec) × (Change in velocity) = ρa(V + u) × V. Work done per second = F × u = ρa(V + u) × V × u. Kinetic energy supplied = 1/2 × mass × Vr² = 1/2 × ρa(V + u) × (V + u)². Efficiency η = (Work done/sec) / (K.E. supplied) = [ρa(V + u)Vu] / [1/2 ρa(V+u)³] = 2Vu / (V+u)².

(b) Given u = 30 km/hr = 8.33 m/s, V = 20 m/s, a = 0.02 m². Density of sea water ρ ≈ 1000 kg/m³ (assuming standard unless specified). Water drawn amid-ship implies inlet at right angles. Propelling force F = ρa(V+u)V = 1000 × 0.02 × (20 + 8.33) × 20 = 11332 N. Efficiency η = (2Vu) / (V+u)² = (2 × 20 × 8.33) / (20 + 8.33)² = 333.2 / 802.58 = 0.415 or 41.5%.

essay.q: Problem 17.1: Find the force exerted by a jet of water of diameter 75 mm on a stationary flat plate, when the jet strikes the plate normally with velocity of 20 m/s.
essay.a:
Given:
Diameter of jet, d = 75 mm = 0.075 m
Area, a = (π/4)d² = (π/4)(0.075)² = 0.004417 m²
Velocity of jet, V = 20 m/s
The force exerted by the jet of water on a stationary vertical plate is given by equation (17.1) as
F = ρaV²
Where ρ = 1000 kg/m³
F = 1000 × 0.004417 × 20² = 1766.8 N. Ans.

essay.q: Problem 17.5: A jet of water of diameter 50 mm moving with a velocity of 40 m/s, strikes a curved fixed symmetrical plate at the centre. Find the force exerted by the jet of water in the direction of the jet, if the jet is deflected through an angle of 120° at the outlet of the curved plate.
essay.a:
Given:
Diameter of the jet, d = 50 mm = 0.05 m
Area, a = (π/4)(0.05)² = 0.001963 m²
Velocity of jet, V = 40 m/s
Angle of deflection = 120°
From equation [17.6 (A)], the angle of deflection = 180° - θ
180° - θ = 120°  =>  θ = 180° - 120° = 60°
Force exerted by the jet on the curved plate in the direction of the jet is given by equation (17.5) as
F_x = ρaV² [1 + cos θ]
= 1000 × 0.001963 × 40² × [1 + cos 60°] = 4711.15 N. Ans.

essay.q: Problem 17.9: A rectangular plate, weighing 58.86 N is suspended vertically by a hinge on the top horizontal edge. The centre of gravity of the plate is 10 cm from the hinge. A horizontal jet of water 2 cm diameter, whose axis is 15 cm below the hinge impinges normally on the plate with a velocity of 5 m/s. Find the horizontal force applied at the centre of gravity to maintain the plate in its vertical position.
essay.a:
Given:
Weight of plate, W = 58.86 N
Distance of W from hinge, x = 10 cm = 0.1 m
Diameter of jet, d = 2 cm = 0.02 m
Area, a = (π/4)d² = (π/4) × 0.02² = 0.000314 m²
Distance of the axis of the jet of water from hinge = 15 cm = 0.15 m
Velocity of jet, V = 5 m/s
The force exerted by a jet of water on the vertical plate,
F = ρaV² = 1000 × 0.000314 × 5² = 7.85 N
This force F is acting at a distance of 15 cm or 0.15 m from the hinge. Let P be the horizontal force acting at C.G.
Taking moments about hinge, we get
F × 0.15 = P × 0.10
P = (F × 0.15) / 0.10 = (7.85 × 0.15) / 0.10 = 11.775 N. Ans.

essay.q: Problem 17.14: A jet of water of diameter 7.5 cm strikes a curved plate at its centre with a velocity of 20 m/s. The curved plate is moving with a velocity of 8 m/s in the direction of the jet. The jet is deflected through an angle of 165°. Assuming the plate smooth find: (i) Force exerted on the plate in the direction of jet, (ii) Power of the jet, and (iii) Efficiency of the jet.
essay.a:
Given:
Diameter of the jet, d = 7.5 cm = 0.075 m
Area, a = (π/4)(0.075)² = 0.004417 m²
Velocity of the jet, V = 20 m/s
Velocity of the plate, u = 8 m/s
Angle of deflection of the jet = 165°
Angle made by the relative velocity at the outlet of the plate, θ = 180° - 165° = 15°
(i) Force exerted by the jet on the plate in the direction of the jet is given by equation (17.17) as
F_x = ρa(V - u)² (1 + cos θ)
= 1000 × 0.004417 × (20 - 8)² [1 + cos 15°] = 1250.38 N. Ans.
(ii) Work done by the jet on the plate per second
= F_x × u = 1250.38 × 8 = 10003.04 N m/s
Power of the jet = 10003.04 / 1000 = 10 kW. Ans.
(iii) Efficiency of the jet = Output / Input = (Work done by jet/sec) / (Kinetic energy of jet/sec)
= (1250.38 × 8) / (½ ρaV³)
= 10003.04 / (½ × 1000 × 0.004417 × 20³) = 0.564 = 56.4%. Ans.

essay.q: Problem 17.26: A jet of water having a velocity of 30 m/s strikes a series of radial curved vanes mounted on a wheel which is rotating at 200 r.p.m. The jet makes an angle of 20° with the tangent to the wheel at inlet and leaves the wheel with a velocity of 5 m/s at an angle of 130° to the tangent to the wheel at outlet. Water is flowing from outward in a radial direction. The outer and inner radii of the wheel are 0.5 m and 0.25 m respectively. Determine: (i) Vane angles at inlet and outlet, (ii) Work done per unit weight of water, and (iii) Efficiency of the wheel.
essay.a:
Given:
Velocity of jet, V1 = 30 m/s
Speed of wheel, N = 200 r.p.m.
Angular speed, ω = 2πN / 60 = (2π × 200) / 60 = 20.94 rad/s
Angle of jet at inlet, α = 20°
Velocity of jet at outlet, V2 = 5 m/s
Angle made by the jet at outlet with the tangent to wheel = 130°
Angle β = 180° - 130° = 50°
Outer radius, R1 = 0.5 m
Inner radius, R2 = 0.25 m
Velocity u1 = ω × R1 = 20.94 × 0.5 = 10.47 m/s
Velocity u2 = ω × R2 = 20.94 × 0.25 = 5.235 m/s
(i) Vane angles at inlet and outlet (θ and φ):
From inlet velocity triangle,
Vw1 = V1 cos α = 30 × cos 20° = 28.19 m/s
Vf1 = V1 sin α = 30 × sin 20° = 10.26 m/s
tan θ = Vf1 / (Vw1 - u1) = 10.26 / (28.19 - 10.47) = 10.26 / 17.72 = 0.579 = tan 30.07°
θ = 30.07° or 30° 4.2'. Ans.
From outlet velocity triangle,
Vw2 = V2 cos β = 5 × cos 50° = 3.214 m/s
Vf2 = V2 sin β = 5 × sin 50° = 3.83 m/s
tan φ = Vf2 / (u2 + Vw2) = 3.83 / (5.235 + 3.214) = 0.453 = tan 24.385°
φ = 24.385° or 24° 23.1'. Ans.
(ii) Work done per second by water is given by equation (17.26)
= ρaV1 [Vw1 u1 + Vw2 u2]
Work done per second per unit weight of water striking per second
= 1/g [Vw1 u1 + Vw2 u2] Nm/N
= 1/9.81 [28.19 × 10.47 + 3.214 × 5.235]
= 1/9.81 [295.15 + 16.82] = 31.8 Nm/N. Ans.
(iii) Efficiency, η is given by equation (17.28) as
η = (2 [Vw1 u1 + Vw2 u2]) / V1²
= (2 [295.15 + 16.82]) / 30² = 0.6932 or 69.32%. Ans.

essay.q: Problem 17.32: A jet propelled boat, moving with a velocity of 5 m/s, draws water amid-ship. The water is discharged through two jets provided at the back of the ship. The diameter of each jet is 150 mm. The total resistance offered to the motion of the boat is 4905 N. Determine: (i) Volume of water drawn by the pump per second, and (ii) Efficiency of the jet propulsion.
essay.a:
Given:
Velocity of boat, u = 5 m/s
Diameter of each jet, d = 150 mm = 0.15 m
Area of each jet = (π/4)(0.15)² = 0.01767 m²
Total area of the jets, a = 2 × 0.01767 = 0.03534 m²
Total resistance to motion = 4905 N
The propelling force must be equal to the resistance to the motion.
Propelling force, F = 4905 N
Propelling force is given by equation (17.33) as
F = ρa(V + u) V
4905 = 1000 × 0.03534 × (V + 5) × V
or 3.6 V² + 18V - 500 = 0
The above equation is quadratic and its solution is
V = [-18 ± √(18² + 4 × 3.6 × 500)] / (2 × 3.6)
= [-18 ± 86.74] / 7.2
= (86.74 - 18) / 2 = 34.37 m/s (as per text)
(i) Volume of water drawn by the pump per second is equal to the volume of water discharged through the orifices at the back in the form of jets and this volume
= a(V + u) = 0.03534 × (34.37 + 5.0) = 1.39 m³/s. Ans.
(ii) Efficiency of the jet propulsion is given by equation (17.31) as
η = 2Vu / (V + u)² = (2 × 34.37 × 5.0) / (34.37 + 5.0)² = 0.2217 or 22.17%. Ans.
